prompt: Which colour order identifies a west cardinal, from top to bottom?
why: West has yellow above and below a broad black middle band. Black–yellow–black is east; black above yellow is north.

prompt: Which topmark belongs to a west cardinal?
options: Two black cones with their points facing together
Two black cones with their bases together
Two black cones both pointing down
why: West has two cones point-to-point. Base-to-base is east; both points down is south.

prompt: Your boat changes heading. What does the west cardinal still indicate?
options: Water to the boat’s port side
Water to the boat’s starboard side
The deepest water in the mark’s area lies to its west
why: Cardinal directions are geographic. West remains west regardless of your heading. Use the chart to determine the actual track, depth and clearance.

prompt: Which white light characteristic is used by a west cardinal?
options: A group of nine very quick flashes every 10 seconds, or nine quick flashes every 15 seconds
Six quick flashes followed by one long flash
why: West is nine on the clock face: VQ(9) 10s or Q(9) 15s. Three identifies east; six plus a long flash identifies south.
